selection.method: highest remaining verified actor-primary profiles after Batch 24

profiles.name: Eleanor Naylor Caughron
profiles.excerpt: Eleanor Naylor Caughron was one of the principal dramatic voices of Dark Fantasy, the Oklahoma City supernatural anthology that reached the NBC network in 1941 and 1942.
profiles.bio_html:
Eleanor Naylor Caughron worked in Oklahoma City radio and became one of the leading actresses on Dark Fantasy, the supernatural anthology created at WKY and carried by NBC. The series relied heavily on a compact local company rather than Hollywood stars.

Caughron was frequently heard in leading roles opposite Ben Morris, moving from frightened wives and romantic leads to women caught in stories of science fiction, horror and the supernatural. Her repeated casting made her one of the program's defining voices.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 16 Dark Fantasy performances credited to Caughron, giving the archive a substantial record of her contribution to one of radio's distinctive regional network productions.

profiles.name: Ethel Everett
profiles.excerpt: Ethel Everett was a New York radio repertory actress whose surviving work stretches from Columbia Workshop and The Shadow to Johnny Dollar and Theater Five.
profiles.bio_html:
Ethel Everett belonged to the New York radio repertory across several generations of dramatic broadcasting. Her surviving credits place her in experimental anthology, mystery, wartime drama and later network revival productions.

Everett appeared on Columbia Workshop, The Shadow, Words at War and X Minus One, then continued into Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar and Theater Five. That span reflects a working actress able to adapt as radio drama changed around her.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves seven Theater Five performances credited to Everett, three Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar appearances, two each on Columbia Workshop and The Shadow, and additional anthology work.

profiles.name: Hetty Galen
profiles.excerpt: Hetty Galen carried a long voice-acting career into CBS Radio Mystery Theater, where she became a recurring repertory performer during radio drama’s 1970s revival.
profiles.bio_html:
Hetty Galen was born in Brooklyn in 1929 and built a career in radio, film, television and voice work. Her later screen appearances were relatively small, but the microphone gave her a much larger range of characters.

Galen worked on Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar and X Minus One before becoming a recurring member of CBS Radio Mystery Theater. She also supplied voices for animated productions during the 1960s and 1970s, extending the same vocal versatility beyond radio.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 13 CBS Radio Mystery Theater performances credited to Galen, two Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar appearances and one X Minus One broadcast.

profiles.name: John Hoyt
profiles.excerpt: John Hoyt brought a sharp, educated character voice to radio suspense before becoming a familiar film and television authority figure.
profiles.bio_html:
John Hoyt was born John McArthur Hoysradt in New York in 1904 and graduated from Yale before entering professional performance. He built a long career in stage, radio, film and television, often playing doctors, officials, scientists and other men of authority.

Radio used Hoyt heavily in suspense and adventure. He appeared repeatedly on Escape and The Whistler, with additional work on Suspense and Jeff Regan, Investigator. Later screen audiences knew him from films and television including an early Star Trek role.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves six performances each on Escape and The Whistler credited to Hoyt, three Suspense appearances and one Jeff Regan, Investigator broadcast.

profiles.name: Lou Marcelle
profiles.excerpt: Lou Marcelle combined station announcing with dramatic performance and became closely associated with the 1930s radio serial The Shadow of Fu Manchu.
profiles.bio_html:
Lou Marcelle worked professionally as a radio announcer in Los Angeles, including staff announcing at KFWB, while also taking acting assignments. His career belongs to the era when station voices regularly moved between announcing, narration and dramatic parts.

Marcelle became strongly associated with the syndicated serial The Shadow of Fu Manchu, recorded in Hollywood in 1938 and 1939. The production drew on experienced West Coast radio actors and announcers for its continuing adventure format.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 16 Fu Manchu performances credited to Marcelle. His professional announcing work is retained as a second category because it formed a substantial part of his broadcasting career.

profiles.name: Myron McCormick
profiles.excerpt: Myron McCormick moved easily between radio drama and Broadway, winning a Tony Award for South Pacific while remaining a strong microphone character actor.
profiles.bio_html:
Myron McCormick was born in Indiana in 1908 and developed into a major stage and radio actor. He worked steadily on Broadway and became widely known as Luther Billis in the original production of South Pacific, a performance that won him a Tony Award in 1950.

Radio used McCormick in serious drama as well as suspense. He appeared repeatedly on Inner Sanctum Mysteries and also worked on Columbia Workshop, Words at War, Lights Out and Suspense, bringing the same stage discipline to microphone roles.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves ten Inner Sanctum Mysteries performances credited to McCormick, two each on Columbia Workshop and Words at War, plus appearances on Lights Out and Suspense.

profiles.name: Sam Buffington
profiles.excerpt: Sam Buffington gave late network radio one of its final western leads as the title character in Luke Slaughter of Tombstone.
profiles.bio_html:
Sam Buffington was born in Massachusetts in 1931 and trained at the Leland Powers School of Radio and Theater. His career moved quickly through stage, radio, television and film during the 1950s.

Buffington's defining radio role was Luke Slaughter, a former cavalryman turned Arizona cattleman, in CBS's 1958 western Luke Slaughter of Tombstone. The series arrived near the end of network radio's western era and gave Buffington a rare continuing lead.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 12 Luke Slaughter of Tombstone performances credited to Buffington, documenting the central radio role of a career that ended while he was still only twenty-eight.

profiles.name: Stephen Chase
profiles.excerpt: Stephen Chase was a stage and screen character actor whose radio work centered on NBC University Theater and literary drama.
profiles.bio_html:
Stephen Chase was born Guy Alden Chase on Long Island in 1902 and worked under several professional names, including Alden Chase, Steve Chase and Steven Chase. He built a long screen and stage career before becoming familiar to later audiences through films such as The Blob.

Radio placed Chase most often in formal dramatic adaptation. NBC University Theater became the strongest concentration of his surviving work, with additional appearances on The Whistler and Let George Do It.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 13 NBC University Theater performances credited under the source form Steven Chase, two The Whistler appearances and one Let George Do It broadcast. His public profile uses the canonical professional form Stephen Chase.

profiles.name: Alan Hewitt
profiles.excerpt: Alan Hewitt carried a long Broadway and screen career into science-fiction and mystery radio from X Minus One to CBS Radio Mystery Theater.
profiles.bio_html:
Alan Hewitt was born in New York in 1915 and built a long career on stage, television and film, usually as polished supporting characters whose authority could be comic, sympathetic or threatening.

Radio gave Hewitt a similarly broad range. He appeared repeatedly on X Minus One and later joined CBS Radio Mystery Theater, with additional work on Molle Mystery Theatre, Theater Five, CBS Radio Workshop and Columbia Workshop.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves five CBS Radio Mystery Theater performances credited to Hewitt, four X Minus One appearances, two each on Molle Mystery Theatre and Theater Five, and additional anthology work.

profiles.name: Anne Diamond
profiles.excerpt: Anne Diamond Brownstone was a prolific Hollywood radio actress who also wrote and directed for early television before returning to stage work later in life.
profiles.bio_html:
Anne Diamond Brownstone was born in 1923 and became a prolific actress during the height of Hollywood radio. She worked opposite major stars across dramatic, comedy and western programs and also became a regular performer at the Pasadena Playhouse.

Diamond's career was broader than acting alone. She wrote for early television and received directing credits, including work in the emerging television industry of the late 1940s and 1950s. Those professional activities support writing and directing as genuine secondary categories.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves four Screen Directors Playhouse performances credited to Anne Diamond, three NBC University Theater appearances and additional work across crime, suspense, western and comedy series.
